title: Zachary Cramton
text:
Zachary Cramton
Spatial Data for Resilient, Livable Communities

LinkedIn GitHub Email


Fourmile Creek, Fairplay, CO ©2026 Zachary Cramton





The greatest potential to improve daily life is in the places people live and build, where environmental damage is concentrated and the most people feel its effects. Restoring remote forests and habitat is important for the broader environment, but it doesn’t always have the visible, direct impact needed to build support and funding for future projects.
I studied Ecosystem Science and Sustainability at Colorado State University, specializing in climate resilience and public education. My work includes transportation planning, environmental analysis, and GIS projects. I have directed $1.5 million in matching funds to successful grant applications totaling over $7 million for multimodal transportation infrastructure.
Recently I’ve led a web and records overhaul for CSU’s Alternative Transportation Fee Advisory Board, authored a micromobility impact report for the Association for Commuter Transportation, and developed a spatial screening tool for beaver conflict and restoration analysis in ArcGIS Pro with ArcPy and the Spatial Analysis Toolbox. My capstone project piloted the migration of NASA GLOBE Observer’s Mosquito Habitat Mapper to the CitSci platform in Fort Collins.

Featured



Spring 2026


Beaver Conflict & Restoration Analysis Tool

ArcGIS Pro Python Spatial Analysis Hydrology

A spatial screening tool built in Python for ArcGIS Pro that intersects BRAT stream network capacity data with NLCD land cover to score stream segments by human-beaver conflict risk and restoration opportunity. Designed to support planning decisions at the county, watershed, or custom AOI scale using ESRI Living Atlas services as default inputs.

GitHub





Spring 2026


CSU Micromobility TDM Impact Report

Transportation Demand Management Micromobility Policy

Authored the 2025 Transportation Demand Management Impact Report entry for Colorado State University’s micromobility program on behalf of ATFAB and CSU Transportation, published by the Association for Commuter Transportation. The report documents ridership data, program outcomes, and policy recommendations for campus active transportation infrastructure.

Full Report (PDF) CSU Feature (p. 22)





Capstone · Spring 2026


NASA GLOBE Observer — CitSci Migration

Citizen Science Data Management Urban Ecology

Piloting the migration of NASA GLOBE Observer’s Mosquito Habitat Mapper to the CitSci platform to explore opportunities to improve data redundancy and expand community reporting capacity in Fort Collins. The final report documents project outcomes, platform assessment, stakeholder engagement, and ongoing implementation challenges.

Seeing Cities Clearly

Feature Article Urban Planning GIS AI

A feature article exploring how AI-powered drone remote sensing and machine learning are transforming urban planning and disaster resilience. Examines real-world applications in land-use classification, urban forest management, historic preservation, and disaster risk mapping.

CO 301B · July 2025


Concrete Jungles

Advance Article Urban Ecology Environmental Justice

More Work



Spring 2026


The Spoke — Knowledge Database

Process Management Record Keeping SOPs

Designed and built an internal knowledge database for The Spoke, CSU’s on-campus bike cooperative, consolidating product documentation, service history frameworks, parts sourcing references, and operational procedures into a structured, searchable system for volunteer mechanics and staff.




2024–2025


ATFAB Web Redesign & Records System

Web Design Public Communication Transportation

Led a comprehensive web redesign and records overhaul for CSU’s Alternative Transportation Fee Advisory Board. Rebuilt the public-facing site for clarity and accessibility, and developed an internal knowledge database to standardize institutional records, meeting documentation, and policy tracking across board transitions.




Spring 2025


Life Cycle Assessment — Soap Refill Packaging

LCA Sustainability Science OpenLCA ecoinvent

A comparative life cycle inventory and impact assessment of plastic bottle versus laminate pouch soap refill containers, using OpenLCA with the ecoinvent 3.11 database and ReCiPe 2016 midpoint methodology. Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis was used to evaluate result robustness. Findings suggest refill pouches carry equal or greater environmental impact than bottles across most impact categories — contrary to common marketing claims.

LCI Report (PDF) LCIA Report (PDF)





Spring 2025


Starship Delivery Robots — Campus Perception Study

Public Engagement Transportation Sustainability Mixed Method Research

A mixed-methods study assessing student perceptions of Starship food delivery robots at CSU using in-person interviews, Likert-scale surveys, and thematic analysis. Findings revealed predominantly negative sentiment centered on inefficiency, resource misprioritization, and concerns that the robots displace more sustainable alternatives like walking and cycling.
